evidence.evidence_paraphrase: Au@Cu2O–Ag core–shell–satellite nanocomposites were tested with different Ag contents; SERS intensity increased through AC–Ag3 and decreased for AC–Ag4.
The paper attributes enhancement to localized electromagnetic fields in gaps between Ag nanocrystals and to the number of hotspot sites.
FDTD modeling and charge-transfer discussion link the ternary Au/Cu2O/Ag structure to enhanced SERS, but not to a controlled polymer-defined gap dimension.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper contains relevant Au/Ag nanostructures, Ag-mediated interparticle hotspots, and SERS intensity variation with Ag loading, but it does not study the polymer-separated Ag-bridge architecture or controlled variation of a polymer-defined inner/outer Ag gap. The reported response is therefore component- and mechanism-level overlap rather than support for the architecture-specific directional relation.

evidence.evidence_paraphrase: Malachite green solutions at multiple concentrations were adsorbed on AC–Ag3 substrates and measured by SERS; solid malachite green powder spectra were used for comparison in the enhancement-factor analysis.
The recycling experiment concerns visible-light self-cleaning and repeated SERS measurements, not a paired dispersed-to-dried preparation comparison or drying-induced spectral transformation.

assessments.scientific_rationale: The paper measures analyte SERS from solution and separately reports Raman spectra of solid malachite green for enhancement-factor estimation, providing limited solution-versus-solid measurement context. It does not perform a paired solution-to-dried transition on the same analyte-mixed Ag-shell core-satellite preparation, nor does it establish a reproducible normalized peak-distribution or qualitative peak-profile transformation.
